en: to be pretty; to be good-looking

examples.en: That actor has a delicate, pretty face.
Unlike his refined looks, his personality is spirited.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때 곱상해서 여자아이로 오해받았어요.
examples.en: My brother was so delicate-looking as a kid that he was mistaken for a girl.
He looks gentle and fair, but he is really good at sports.
I was complimented for looking fair and delicate.
He had a neat, pretty look, so my first impression was good.

explain: '잘생기다'와 달리 얼굴선이 곱고 순한 인상일 때 써요. 남자에게 쓰면 듣는 사람에 따라 남자다운 느낌이 약하다는 말로 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. '예쁘장하다'와 비슷하지만 더 얌전하고 단정한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My younger brother has a pretty face, so he's popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생김새를 말할 때 '곱상하게 생기다'가 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '곱상하게 생기다' is the common way to talk about someone's looks.

phrases.en: He has a delicate face but a deep voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 쓰는 활용형으로 순하고 고운 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form before a noun describing a soft, fine-featured face.

phrases.en: That child has a pretty face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱상하다'와 비슷하지만 주로 여자아이나 어린 사람에게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 곱상하다 but most often used for girls or young people.

explain_en: Unlike '잘생기다', it is used for a face with soft, delicate lines and a gentle look. Said about a man, some listeners may hear it as 'not very masculine', so be careful. It is similar to '예쁘장하다' but feels more modest and neat.

en: to be completely exhausted; to be absolutely worn out

examples.en: I walked on mountain trails all day and I'm completely worn out.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나고 나니 기진맥진해서 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: After the exam, I'm so exhausted I can't even speak.
The exhausted children fell asleep in the car.
I didn't know I would be this worn out.
After working all night, I'm always completely drained.
When I'm totally exhausted, I don't want to do anything.

explain: '피곤하다'나 '지치다'보다 힘이 완전히 빠진 상태를 강조해요. 달리기, 등산, 야근처럼 몸을 많이 쓴 뒤에 어울려요. '녹초가 되다'도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling came home looking completely exhausted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 지친 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes an exhausted appearance.

phrases.en: I was so exhausted that I couldn't climb the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지친 이유를 말하고 뒤에 결과를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give exhaustion as the reason for what follows.

phrases.en: I'm so tired today because I had a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기진맥진하다'보다 약하고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Milder than '기진맥진하다' and widely used in daily life.

explain_en: It stresses that all your strength is gone, stronger than '피곤하다' or '지치다'. It suits times after heavy physical effort such as running, hiking or overtime. '녹초가 되다' is similar.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 요즘 너무 깡말라 보여요.
examples.en: That actor looks too skinny these days.
He has a bony build, but he is really strong.
My younger brother is so skinny that Mom always worries.
I dieted too hard and became gaunt.

examples.ko: 깡마르다고 해서 건강하지 않은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being very thin doesn't mean being unhealthy.
The old man was very thin, but his eyes were sharp.

explain: '마르다'보다 훨씬 심하게 뼈가 드러날 만큼 여윈 모습이에요. '날씬하다'와 달리 칭찬이 아니에요. 'ㄹ' 때문에 '깡말라요', '깡마른'처럼 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: After being sick, my face became gaunt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 몸이 뼈가 보일 만큼 여윈 모습이에요. '깡마른'으로 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A face or body so thin that bones show. '깡마른' modifies a noun.

phrases.en: The cat is skin and bones, as if it hasn't eaten for days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㄹ' 때문에 '깡말랐어요'로 바뀌어요. 지금 상태가 아주 말랐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because of the 'ㄹ' it becomes '깡말랐어요'. It says someone is extremely thin now.

phrases.en: I've lost a lot of weight lately because of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 비슷한 말이에요. '깡마르다'보다 훨씬 약하고 중립적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, similar phrase. It is much milder and more neutral than '깡마르다'.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '마르다' and means so thin that the bones show. Unlike '날씬하다', it is not a compliment. Because of the ㄹ, it changes to forms like '깡말라요' and '깡마른'.

examples.en: I woke up and my face looks haggard.
My hair was rough, so I bought a treatment.
His face has become quite haggard in a few days.
I feel bad touching the baby with my rough hands.
I was tired and went to work looking worn out.
I washed a puppy with coarse fur.

explain: '거칠다'와 비슷하지만, 얼굴이나 피부가 마르고 윤기가 없어서 피곤해 보인다는 느낌이 자주 들어가요. '얼굴이 꺼칠해지다'는 건강이 안 좋아 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 어제 야근을 해서 오늘 얼굴이 꺼칠해 보여요.
phrases.en: I worked late yesterday, so my face looks haggard today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피곤하거나 건강이 좋지 않아서 얼굴이 거칠고 지쳐 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a face looks rough and worn out from tiredness or poor health.

phrases.en: A moisturizing cream is good for rough skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 거칠고 윤기 없는 피부를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes skin that is rough and dull.

phrases.en: I caught a cold and my face looks worn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아지다'를 붙여 상태가 나빠졌다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아지다' it means the condition has gotten worse.
phrases.en_equiv: for one's face to look worn

explain_en: It is similar to '거칠다' (rough), but often carries a sense of dry, dull skin that makes someone look tired. '얼굴이 꺼칠해지다' is what you say when someone looks unwell.

en: to be spotless; to be impeccable; to be unhurt

examples.en: I played all night, but my mind is still clear.

examples.ko: 넘어졌는데 다친 데 없이 몸이 말짱했어요.
examples.en: I fell down, but my body was fine without any injury.

examples.ko: 세탁했는데도 옷이 말짱한 걸 보니 소재가 좋은가 봐요.
examples.en: The clothes look fine even after washing, so the fabric must be good.
The computer that was working fine suddenly shut off.
You said you were sick, but your face looks perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 겉은 말짱해 보여도 속은 다 상했어요.
examples.en: It looks intact on the outside, but it's all spoiled inside.

explain: '멀쩡하다'와 비슷하게 다치거나 망가진 데 없이 온전할 때 써요. '정신이 말짱하다'처럼 졸리거나 흐릿하지 않고 또렷하다는 뜻으로도 많이 말해요. 사람의 몸, 물건, 정신 상태에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The cars collided, but the people are fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말짱하다와 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 말짱하다 and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My cold is all gone and I feel fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아프거나 다친 데가 없이 괜찮은 몸 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a body with no illness or injury.

phrases.en: I drank coffee, so my mind is clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸리거나 흐릿하지 않고 정신이 또렷할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when your mind is clear, not sleepy or foggy.

explain_en: Like '멀쩡하다', it is used when something or someone is intact, without injury or damage. It is also commonly used for a clear mind, as in '정신이 말짱하다', meaning not sleepy or hazy. It works for a person's body, objects and mental state.

examples.en: I had a simple procedure at the dermatology clinic.

examples.ko: 이 시술은 흉터가 거의 안 남아요.
examples.en: This procedure leaves almost no scar.

examples.ko: 시술 후에는 일주일 동안 운동하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: After the procedure, you shouldn't exercise for a week.
How much would the procedure cost?

examples.ko: 어머니는 눈 시술을 받고 훨씬 편해지셨어요.
examples.en: My mother felt much better after getting an eye treatment.

examples.ko: 어떤 시술이 저한테 맞을지 의사 선생님께 여쭤봤어요.
examples.en: I asked the doctor which procedure would suit me.

explain: '수술'은 몸을 크게 열어서 하는 치료이고, '시술'은 피부를 조금만 건드리거나 주사·레이저로 하는 가벼운 치료에 많이 써요. 보통 '시술을 받다', '시술을 하다'로 말해요. 병원 광고에서는 피부·미용 이야기에 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I had a procedure at the hospital yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료를 받는 사람이 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for the person receiving the treatment.

phrases.en: After the procedure, be careful when washing your face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 끝난 뒤를 말해요. 병원 안내에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the time after treatment. Often heard in hospital instructions.

phrases.en: The procedure takes about thirty minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료에 걸리는 시간을 말할 때 써요. 예약할 때 많이 물어봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how long the treatment takes. A common question when booking.

explain_en: 수술 (surgery) usually means opening the body, while 시술 is used for lighter treatments done with injections, lasers, or tiny cuts. People say '시술을 받다' (to get a procedure) or '시술을 하다' (to perform one). You will see it a lot in clinic ads, especially for skin and beauty treatments.

examples.en: My grandfather is still active and energetic.
Kids have a hearty appetite, so they eat a lot.
When spring comes, the trees grow vigorously.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 왕성한 창작 활동으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That writer is famous for his prolific creative work.

examples.ko: 호기심이 왕성한 학생이 질문을 많이 해요.
examples.en: A student with great curiosity asks many questions.
You have to be healthy for your stamina to be strong.

explain: '왕성하다'는 식욕, 호기심, 활동처럼 힘이 넘쳐서 활발할 때 써요. '건강하다'는 몸 상태 전체를 말하고, '왕성하다'는 그 힘이 눈에 띄게 드러난다는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '식욕이 왕성하다', '왕성한 활동'처럼 짝이 정해져 있어요.

phrases.example: 아이들은 왕성한 호기심으로 질문을 많이 해요.
phrases.en: Children ask many questions out of their strong curiosity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호기심이 아주 많고 활발할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for very active, abundant curiosity.

phrases.en: My appetite has grown strong since I started exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래보다 입맛이 더 좋아졌다는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a change where the appetite gets stronger.

phrases.en: Thanks to the spring rain, the grass grows vigorously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물이 힘 있게 잘 자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when plants grow vigorously.

explain_en: '왕성하다' is used when appetite, curiosity or activity is overflowing with energy. '건강하다' describes overall condition, while '왕성하다' implies the vitality is clearly visible. It usually pairs with fixed words, as in '식욕이 왕성하다' or '왕성한 활동'.
